clinician.trajectory_summary: A 6-year-old girl with relapsed adrenal neuroblastoma (INSS stage 4, unfavorable histology) who had undergone prior left adrenalectomy and left nephrectomy developed febrile neutropenia after 3 courses of second-line cisplatin-based chemotherapy. She presented with persistent fever unresponsive to broad-spectrum antibiotics, abdominal pain, and hepatosplenomegaly. Blood culture identified Candida sp., indicating disseminated candidiasis. Abdominal ultrasound revealed focal, nonhomogeneous, hypoechoic nodular splenic lesions (up to 2 cm) that were radiologically indeterminate between fungal abscess and tumor recurrence. PET/CT imaging showed focal hypermetabolic splenic areas (SUVmax 3.2) suggesting inflammatory processes but not definitively excluding tumor involvement. A splenic procedure (splenectomy) was performed. Histopathological analysis of the splenic specimen confirmed candidiasis, demonstrating only chronic inflammatory process without any malignant cells or evidence of neuroblastoma recurrence, thereby ruling out metastatic disease.
